title: Dreyer et al. 2023 — A large EEG database with users' profile information for motor imagery brain-computer interface research
description: A large EEG database of 87 healthy participants performing a right- versus left-hand motor imagery brain-computer interface task in a single-day session, organized into three datasets (A, B, C) recorded with the same Graz protocol. Each participant completed 240 trials (over 20,800 in total). The database includes demographics, personality profile and cognitive trait information. It supports studies of the relationship between user profile and BCI performance, and the design of cross-user classification algorithms.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 512 Hz with a g.USBAmp amplifier (g.tec) and active electrodes: 27 EEG channels, plus EOG and EMG channels, referenced to the left earlobe with ground at FPz. Participants completed 6 runs (2 calibration runs with sham feedback and 4 online training runs with real continuous visual feedback) of 40 trials each. Online processing used participant-specific discriminant frequency band selection (5-35 Hz), a fifth-order Butterworth filter, CSP spatial filtering and an LDA classifier. Questionnaires assessed demographics, personality (16PF5), cognitive traits, spatial abilities and learning style.
